scope: Only T4 and T5 supplemented; T1/T2/T3/T6 and the 14-test regression were not rerun.
environmentCorrection: The user's authenticated Chrome page at port 3080 used a separate Web profile without Wish Willow. Missing entry there was not treated as a plugin defect. With explicit user approval, reused the previously installed isolated GitHub profile and started a full official Web runtime on 3081; both test windows used that one Host.
authentication: The isolated launcher passes the official newly generated authenticatedUrl directly to Chrome, as the official startup handoff does; it is not printed or saved. Existing secrets, cookies and credential files were not extracted. An ordinary config overlay disables printing/opening by the default-browser handoff, not the authentication checks.
automation: Windows UI Automation targets actual Chrome-rendered controls using their accessibility properties, real Invoke/Value actions and guarded foreground keystrokes. Screenshots use target-only PrintWindow with browser toolbars redacted. Product writes occur only through the real page, never by editing JSON or calling a substitute/mock API.
nonProductProbeFailures: Web Settings exposed ExpandCollapse rather than Invoke; the unsupported action failed before input and the supported pattern was used.

The initial browser discovery script's literal Chinese control name was misdecoded by Windows PowerShell. Replaced only that test-script literal with code points; then identified exact origins and distinct window handles.

Fresh isolated DSH displays optional model-key onboarding, including after a full refresh. Used the built-in Configure later option; configured no API key and made no model call. A few navigation commands ran before that UI transition was ready and stopped on zero matches; observed the page before continuing.

Two exploratory keystroke/clamping assertions failed: bulk SendKeys(121 X) yielded length 60 at inspection; ValuePattern(119 X) plus three paced keys yielded 122, not the assumed 120. These probes DO NOT prove native per-keystroke maxLength clamping. Their raw snapshots are retained. The actual validation acceptance uses oversized values entered through accessibility, a real Save click, visible invalid-input feedback, preserved draft and unchanged committed disk bytes. No product code or existing regression assertion was relaxed or modified.

verifierCorrection.initialRun: 19 passed / 1 failed, exit 1; results.json and verification.log retained unchanged, original verifier preserved as verify-results-initial.py.
verifierCorrection.cause: Verifier assumed UIA would serialize all 10001 supplied textarea characters. Actual ValuePattern snapshot exposed 10000, while the invalid-input alert was present and committed data remained unchanged.
verifierCorrection.additionalEvidence: Repeated only this invalid-wish check, recording the visible draft before Save and after the error: both 10000 characters, exactly equal. No product change. Real validation/error and non-persistence assertions remain required.
verifierCorrection.finalRun: 20 passed / 0 failed, exit 0; results-final.json and verification-final.log. Native per-keystroke clamping is not claimed.

boundaries: T5 uses two real browser windows/independent page states, not one Desktop window plus one Web window. Distinct window handles and different simultaneous drafts/revisions establish separate clients on one Web Host.
No claim of cross-Host CAS, every mobile viewport, all accessibility input methods or all browser engines.
Existing production data is read only for hash checks. Test product remains in an isolated storage root.
